verdict.label: not_comparable
verdict.rationale: Study A prospectively examines the inverse association between serum adiponectin and incident metabolic syndrome in postmenopausal women with obesity, reporting no inverse association (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.27-1.14). Study B is a cross-sectional study of Chinese women with PCOS reporting an independent (adjusted) association of serum adiponectin with metabolic syndrome (p = 0.020) without a stated direction. The populations (postmenopausal women with obesity vs PCOS women), designs (prospective incidence vs cross-sectional prevalence), and outcome contrasts (incident metabolic syndrome vs prevalent metabolic syndrome) differ, and Study B does not report a directional estimate, so the findings cannot be meaningfully compared.

source_evidence.quote: However, the inverse association between serum adiponectin levels and incidence of metabolic syndrome was observed in premenopausal women with obesity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03-0.81), but not in postmenopausal women with obesity (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.27-1.14).
Serum adiponectin is independently associated with the metabolic syndrome in Chinese women with PCOS.

diagnostics.notes: Both claims concern serum adiponectin and metabolic syndrome, but the populations and outcome contrasts differ: A is a prospective cohort of women without metabolic syndrome at baseline examining incident metabolic syndrome in postmenopausal women with obesity, while B is a cross-sectional study of Chinese women with PCOS examining prevalent metabolic syndrome. Additionally, B reports only an independent association with p = 0.020 and no directional estimate, whereas A reports a directional (inverse) association that was not confirmed. These differences prevent a meaningful comparison of the findings.
